long_description.before:
Mito Health is a U.S. service that lets individuals order more than 1,000 laboratory markers, panels, scans, and at-home kits without going through a traditional doctor’s visit. Members pay $9 per month to access every test at the company’s published cost, see itemized receipts with no hidden mark-ups, and receive priority turnaround on results. 

After answering an online questionnaire, users receive personalized test recommendations, can schedule a nearby draw at the lowest available price, and obtain clinician-reviewed action plans that cover sleep, supplements, exercise, and other lifestyle factors. The platform also allows members to upload past lab data, view longitudinal trends, and chat year-round with clinicians or AI health coaching through the built-in Mito Concierge.
long_description.after:
Mito Health is a U.S. service that lets individuals order 12,000+ lab tests, scans, supplements, genetics, home kits, and Rx without a traditional doctor’s visit. Members pay $9 per month to access every product at cost and get itemized receipts with no hidden markups.

The average member saves about $300 a year on a full baseline panel.

What the $9/mth Mito membership gets you:

- 11,000+ practitioner-grade supplements at 35% below Amazon (Thorne, Pure Encapsulations, Life Extension, Ritual, Momentous, Seed)
- 1,200+ lab tests from Quest, Labcorp and BioReference at cost · 49 states · HSA/FSA eligible
- DEXA body composition, bone density, coronary calcium (CAC), whole-body MRI, 30x whole genome sequencing, gut microbiome, multi-cancer early detection
- Every result in one longitudinal record, ordered and reviewed by a partner clinician over concierge
- No markups on tests. No commissions from labs or brands.
- No padded "wellness panels," no upsells, no annual contract; you can cancel anytime.

long_description.before: Astro finds and buys land for new renewable energy projects, secures grid connections at minimal cost, and sells these development-ready projects to larger energy companies. Founded by Alex Fuster, a former Citadel energy trader, Astro's AI models identify profitable grid connections that eliminate the surprise costs causing 80-90% of renewable projects to fail. With the U.S. needing 2,000 gigawatts of new power generation by 2035 for AI data centers and electrification, Astro unlocks development opportunities that traditional methods consistently miss.
long_description.after: Astro develops power-ready land for AI data centers. Power is now the bottleneck for new data centers, and Astro’s models find the sites that have it. Founder Alex Fuster traded grid congestion at Citadel across US power markets, predicting where the grid would run out of room.

one_liner.before: The world’s first AI energy developer
one_liner.after: Power-ready land for AI data centers

long_description.before:
Conntour enables organizations to query video - from security cameras, body cams, and drones.

Users can search past footage (“Find a man with tattoos on his left arm”), configure real-time alerts (“Notify me if someone climbs over the wall”), and extract data (“How many pickup trucks entered yesterday?”).

Unlike traditional video analytics solutions, which are limited to fixed parameters (like a weapon, bag, or car color), Conntour supports an unlimited range of highly specific scenarios described in plain language. This enables a single human to monitor thousands of cameras, or find a specific moment in minutes instead of days.

What makes the technology unique is its ability to process video at scale, fully on-prem, with minimal hardware requirements.

Conntour is backed by top-tier investors including General Catalyst and Y Combinator, selected for the first-ever Palantir Fellowship, and advised by Bob Flores - former CTO of the CIA.

long_description.before:
We’re building Stacktrace to help teams see what AI agents actually do, detect risky
behavior, and alert the people responsible. Administrators can also deploy policies that block unapproved tools, such as MCP servers and plugins, before agents use them.
long_description.after:
Agents will do most of the work in the future, but only if teams can trust them unsupervised.
Stacktrace is the control layer for every agent: it sees every action, detects risky behavior, enforces the bounds your team sets, and steps in when an agent drifts from intent.

long_description.before:
Production agents handle many different customer workflows. Currently, when one handles a situation badly, an engineer reads the trace and patches the prompt. The next situation needs another exception. Soon, improving the agent becomes a recurring engineering job, and the prompt keeps growing.

Mirrors finds patterns in past runs and feedback. Engineers review guidance for a specific situation and preview where it would apply. Mirrors then delivers that guidance while the agent works, inside the team’s existing setup. The team can check whether the change improved the outcome.

We’re building Mirrors for engineering teams running customer-facing agents across varied workflows, so they can improve behavior without hardcoding every lesson in the global prompt.

long_description.before: Acyclic runs agent swarms. Hand it a task from the CLI, the dashboard, or a coding agent over MCP, and it splits the work across many agents, each in its own sandbox, then merges what they produce into one result. Long agentic workflows finish in a fraction of the wall-clock time. Bring your own model keys or run the sandboxes in your own cloud; the harness underneath is open source. Coding is the first workload, and research and data work run the same way. Founded by Ram Vinjamuri and Varun Latthe. YC F26, London.
long_description.after:
Acyclic builds the infrastructure for agent swarms: open-source primitives for running agents in parallel, and a managed agents platform that runs swarms for you. Complex, long-running tasks are split across many agents, each working in its own instant fork of the workspace, and finish in a fraction of the time.

We built Acyclic because we believe there are huge gains to be had in how agents are run, beyond the models themselves. Agents can already do real work, but they still do it one step at a time, so complex tasks take hours or days. Running them as swarms is an infrastructure problem: isolating each agent, dividing the work, and merging the results without conflicts. Today, teams use Acyclic to run heavy document-processing pipelines in minutes instead of hours.

At Cambridge, we researched ML and auto-parallelising compilers, and then we built multi-agent systems in production: Ram as a Palantir FDE for pharma clients, shipping systems for clinical trial design, and Varun leading agent architecture at Tracelight for Big 4 accounting firms. We kept asking the same question: the agents were good enough, so why couldn't we run thousands of them at once to make everything faster and cheaper? Acyclic is our answer.

one_liner.before: Rapid agent swarms: make any agentic workflow exponentially faster
one_liner.after: Agent swarms that make long-running tasks exponentially faster
